options: An event $A$ is said to be independent of another event $B$, if $P(A \mid B) \ne P(A)$.
For two events $A$ and $B$, $P(A \cap B) = P(B) \times P(A \mid B)$, where $P(B) > 0$.
For two events $A$ and $B$, $P(A \cap B) = P(A) \times P(B \mid A)$, where $P(A) > 0$.
Events $A$ and $B$ are said to be disjoint if $P(A \cap B) = P(A) \times P(B)$.

questions.context: A city has three main taxi companies: Red Taxi, Blue Taxi, and Green Taxi. Historical data shows that 20% of the passengers use Red Taxi, 50% use Blue Taxi, and 30% use Green Taxi. 5% of the cars from Red Taxi, 4% from Blue Taxi, and 8% from Green Taxi have engine issues.
questions.q: Find the probability that a randomly chosen passenger gets a taxi with engine issues. Enter the answer correct to three decimal places.
